divergences.description: The SSE wire format doesn't match what the plan expected. The plan's StreamDone carries `content` and `createdAt`, the `token` frame has a `delta` field, and on `done` the bloc replaces the content with the server's final text (T008/T012/T022). The code reads the token's text from a `text` field and builds StreamDone from `assistantMessageId` only. The bloc then finalizes the message from the tokens it collected locally, not from server-sent content.
The spec and T017 say the failure text replaces the timestamp ('shown in place of the timestamp'). The failed bubble shows the failure text and still shows the timestamp below it.

The drawer gained an account header that was never planned: an initials avatar plus a display name taken from the email inside the stored JWT. Supporting it, a new `SecureTokenStorage.readAccountEmail()` method was added, and the drawer reads storage directly through getIt.
A new design token, `sizeAvatarMenu`, was added. The plan explicitly says zero new tokens are needed.
The shared Dio instance now has connect, send and receive timeouts set globally. This wasn't in the plan and changes timeout behavior for every API call in the app, not just chat.

After a turn fails with empty content, the bloc makes an extra `listMessages` call and may replace the failed bubble with the server's saved answer (`_reconcileSilentFailure`). This recovery behavior isn't in the plan or the contract.

divergences.description: The SSE wire format differs from the plan. T008/T012/T022 say `token` frames carry `delta` and `done` frames carry `content` and `createdAt`, and that `StreamDone` replaces the message content with the server's own final text. In the diff, the token field is read as `text`, `StreamDone` carries only `assistantMessageId`, and the client keeps its locally accumulated tokens as the final content instead of server text.
A failed message shows the 'Falha ao gerar resposta' note above the timestamp, and the timestamp is still shown. FR-004, T017 and T030 say the note replaces the timestamp.
A new design token, `sizeAvatarMenu`, was added. The plan says zero new tokens are needed (Principle IV and the Constraints section).

An unplanned account header was added to the drawer: an initials avatar and a display name built from the account email. To get the email, a new `SecureTokenStorage.readAccountEmail()` decodes it from the stored JWT on the device. The plan does not include this feature, and it adds a new core API.
Connect, send and receive timeouts were added to the global `Dio` instance. The plan does not include this, and it changes network behavior for every endpoint in the app.

An unplanned `_reconcileSilentFailure` step was added. When a turn fails with empty content, the bloc calls `listMessages` again and may replace the failed bubble with a completed message from the server. This recovery behavior is not in the plan.

A new domain helper, `ChatSessionTimestampFormatter`, was added. It gives side-menu timestamps relative weekday/month formatting in Portuguese. It is not among the 5 domain entities/helpers the plan lists.

divergences.description: SSE event shapes differ from the plan: T008/T012/T022 specify TokenReceived from decoded['delta'] and StreamDone carrying content+createdAt whose server content replaces the locally concatenated tokens. The implementation reads the token field 'text', StreamDone carries only assistantMessageId, and the message is finalized from locally accumulated tokens, following the backend's actual wire contract.
Failed-message indication is rendered above the timestamp (both shown) instead of 'in place of the timestamp' as required by FR-004/US2 scenario 3/T017.
Unplanned behavior: after a turn fails with empty content, ChatBloc performs an extra listMessages refetch and may replace the failed bubble with a completed server message (_reconcileSilentFailure).

Unplanned drawer header: an avatar with initials and a display name derived from the email claim decoded from the stored JWT (new SecureTokenStorage.readAccountEmail), plus a new design token sizeAvatarMenu, although the plan states zero new tokens.
Global Dio BaseOptions timeouts (connect/send 15s, receive 30s) were added for every API call, which was not in the plan and changes app-wide network behavior.
